summary: Lower a derived constructor to a C# base-constructor initializer only when super() is the first semantically observable constructor action.

target.notes: Emit `: base(...)` and place derived-field initialization plus the remaining constructor body after the base constructor returns.

caveats: Even side-effect-only statements before super make C# constructor-initializer lowering observably wrong.

tests.name: simple super forwarding
tests.input: class B { constructor(x){ this.x=x; } } class D extends B { constructor(x){ super(x); this.y=2; } }
tests.expected_csharp: public D(double x) : base(x) { /* derived JS fields */ this.y = 2d; }
tests.expected_behavior: x is set by B, then derived fields initialize, then y is assigned

tests.name: edge: work before super excludes base initializer
tests.input: class B { constructor(){ console.log('base'); } } class D extends B { constructor(){ console.log('before'); super(); } } new D();
tests.expected_behavior: prints before then base; direct C# `: base()` would run base before the derived constructor body and is therefore not equivalent
